# Holub (2003; revised 2012)

**Citation.** Štěpán Holub, “Binary equality sets are generated by two words,”
*Journal of Algebra* **259**(1), 1–42, 2003. Revised author version, arXiv:1209.4061,
2012.

- DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/S0021-8693(02)00534-3
- Canonical revised source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1209.4061
- Local PDF: `holub-2012-binary-equality-sets.pdf`
- Retrieved: 2026-07-24
- SHA-256: `a1258e946cf29c4a0391cc2175874363f7d6365edaf7e7adb101facfb3d55174`

## Results used

For two non-periodic morphisms on a binary source alphabet, the equality set is generated
by at most two words. When it has rank two, its two generators begin and end with
different source letters.

This theorem records the rigidity peculiar to the two-letter equality problem. It does not
decide fixed-boundary `GPCP(3)`, but it warns against extrapolating binary residual
arguments without identifying the structure lost at the third source letter.

## Audit notes

The local file is the author's revised version. It corrects a false strengthening of Lemma 29
in the published paper; the corrected lemma suffices for the main theorem. Any formal use
should follow the revised text, not the journal typesetting alone.
